text_version.version: Consolidated Hebrew text of the Protection of Privacy Law 5741-1981 incorporating amendments through Amendment No. 13 (Sefer HaChukim 5784 p. 1430), revision 3088217

territorial_scope.description: Regulates personal-information databases processed by digital means in Israel, with specific national rules on data transferred to Israel from abroad and on transfers outside Israel (s.36).

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Israel's Protection of Privacy Law 1981, as amended in 2024, binds controllers and processors of personal-information databases: purpose limits, registration, notice, access and correction, information security, data-protection officers and direct-mail rules. The Privacy Protection Authority enforces it via fines, orders, civil damages and criminal penalties.
summary.long: The Protection of Privacy Law 1981 (consolidated text with amendments marked 2024) makes privacy infringement a civil wrong (s.4) and a criminal offence (s.5, five years' imprisonment). For personal-information databases it sets purpose-limited processing (s.8), a registration duty for databases above 10,000 individuals in direct-marketing or sale activities and for public-body databases (s.8A), notice to persons asked for data (s.11), access and correction rights (ss.13-14), and security responsibility with regulations and tiered security levels (s.17, Schedule 3). It requires data-protection officers for public bodies and certain large or sensitive-data controllers (s.17B1), security officers for specified databases (s.17B), regulates direct mailing (ss.17D-17H), and restricts disclosure by public bodies (ss.23B-23D). The Privacy Protection Authority supervises through inspectors and external experts, may seek cease-violation orders and court injunctions, and imposes administrative fines (s.23K; base amount 150,000 new shekels, indexed). Courts may award statutory damages without proof of harm (ss.15A, 29A). Chapter 4A limits enforcement powers against parties and candidates during election periods.

Text issues: s. 3 marks 'שימוש' as deleted, then defines 'עיבוד' and 'שימוש' together; s. 23 para. (3) and the 'מאגר מידע' and 'מידע' entries are deleted; Schedule 3 item (1) contains a drafting note '[צ״ל: פסקה]'. s. 23כ(ב)(2) applies sub-chapters B and C of Chapter D1 to the police from 14.8.2028. Two separate security-body definitions exist: 'רשות בטחון' (s. 19(ג)) and 'גוף ביטחוני' (s. 23כ(א)). Schedule 1 s. 3 also cites Resolution 3543 (2018), which is not in the preamble.
